answer: The sample is committed in advance and revealed afterwards, and identities that signed the sampled transaction cannot verify it, so verification is always performed by a party with no stake in the outcome. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. One walnut is drawn blind, one relic must sign it without stake, and the spiral proves the draw was fair: the farm can file a thousand claims but only the walnut subset is ever checked, and each of those needs a relic it does not own. The verifier must also be independent of the transactor.
